overall: Atlanta is starting the day at a notably elevated 77.0°F at 4 AM with absolutely zero overnight cooling — temperatures have been locked flat at 77.0°F since midnight, indicating thick low-level cloud cover (broken at 427m ceiling, 62% cloud fraction) and a very humid airmass that suppressed radiational cooling entirely. The dewpoint at 73.4°F represents a razor-thin dewpoint depression of only 3.6°F, meaning the atmosphere is near saturation and convective cloud development this afternoon is a real possibility. Despite the oppressive overnight warmth, daytime heating potential is somewhat constrained by the moisture-laden environment.
forecast_obs_notes: There is meaningful spread across NWP models: NBM (80.8°F) is the most conservative, likely capturing convective cloud and boundary-layer moisture effects; ECMWF (83.7°F) sits in the middle; and HRRR (86.2°F) is the most bullish on afternoon heating. max_temp_prediction: The META (fused) model places peak probability at 86–87°F (26.4%), with a weighted expected value near 87°F, while the high-confidence odd-bucket ensemble strongly signals 81–82°F as the most likely single-degree range. Balancing these signals alongside the physical constraints — near-saturated low-level moisture, persistent overnight clouds, and NWP spread of ~5.4°F — the most defensible estimate is in the mid-80s, with a slight downward bias from the moisture cap risk. Confidence is moderate; the key uncertainty is whether convective clouds suppress afternoon heating as NBM and the odd-bucket ensemble suggest, or whether insolation breaks through the overcast as HRRR expects.
